:::{#def-joint-surprisal}
#### Joint surprisal

Let $X$ and $Y$ be discrete random variables
with joint probability mass function $p(x, y) \eqdef \P(X=x, Y=y)$.
The **joint surprisal** of a pair of outcomes $(x, y)$ with $p(x, y) > 0$
is the [surprisal](#def-surprisal) of that pair:

$$s(x, y) \eqdef -\log p(x, y).$$

:::
